title: Stop the upload service from starting without a quota for every tier

blocks.text: The upload service reads one quota per pricing tier from its properties at startup (`quota.FREE=25`, `quota.TEAM=750`, ...). Last quarter's release added the `ENTERPRISE` tier, and the deployment for one region shipped without `quota.ENTERPRISE`. The service started, passed its health checks, and the first enterprise customer's upload failed with a `NullPointerException` two days later. The on-call engineer wants that kind of mistake, and a mistyped tier in a key, to stop the startup with a message that says what to fix.
`load(...)` in `src/main/java/practice/Quotas.java` already reads the file. Finish its two `TODO`s:

items: `checkComplete(...)`: the check that runs before `load` returns.

blocks.text: When you're done, a file that misses a tier, has no quotas at all, or names a tier that doesn't exist fails the load with an `IllegalStateException` that names the problem. About eight lines in total.

cases.says: a complete file gives every tier its quota and other keys are ignored
loading a file that leaves a tier without a quota fails with IllegalStateException naming that tier
loading a file with no quota at all fails with IllegalStateException naming every tier
a quota key that names no tier fails the load with IllegalStateException naming the key

origin.section: Enum-Keyed Configuration Belongs in an EnumMap Checked for Every Key at Startup

concepts: Configuration keyed by an enum is loaded into an EnumMap and checked against EnumSet.allOf before it is used, so a constant without a value stops the startup instead of the first request, and an unknown key is reported by name.
